notes: Scope: reworked packages/world/src/noise/** (perlin.ts, fbm.ts, climate.ts, index.ts) and added packages/world/src/__tests__/world-b.noise.test.ts (28 tests). Exported names, argument order and the NoiseBasis / WarpResult / CreateNoiseBasis shapes from src/internal.ts are unchanged, so src/index.ts, src/terrain/**, src/biome/** and src/features/** compile untouched.

Output is bit-identical to L1-A's v1 for every field. Verified two ways: about 40 pinned values in the new test (perlin2, perlin3, fbm2, fbm3, ridged2, warp2, climateAt, seeds 1337 and 20260916) and an accumulated-sum probe over 5 chunks comparing v1 extracted from 395745d against this tree (job 36a8525b2ffa4082).
golden.json is untouched. golden:update was NOT run and no golden hash changed, because every improvement is structural and value-preserving.

Performance: noise work per chunk went from 1.0981 ms (v1) to 0.9075 ms, 1.21x, saving about 0.19 ms per chunk. For context, world-a's perf test reports full chunkGen averaging 6.471 ms against PERF.chunkGenBudgetMs 4 and BENCH.chunkGenAvgMsMax 6; the rest of that gap is outside the noise layer (column fill, features).

Regression found and fixed inside this task. The first v2 pass (4234e19) hand-inlined the lattice dot products and the interpolation tree and used Int8Array gradient tables. A variant benchmark (job 4c28dd12bc9543ad) showed that made noise 16-19 percent SLOWER than v1, because the sampler bodies grow past what V8 will inline into the fBm octave loops; plain array plus inlining was worst at 1.37x v1. c6dc219 restores the small monomorphic dot2/dot3/lerp helpers and the plain tables, and perlin.ts now carries the measurements in a comment so the inlining is not reintroduced.

Kept from the v2 pass: the *Raw split, so the finite-input check runs once per field sample instead of once per octave; Float64Array scratch buffers in warp2To / warpStages2 / climateAt, removing roughly 512 short-lived WarpResult objects per chunk; and non-finite guards at the public entry points so NaN cannot reach terrain.

Determinism: gradients come only from hashU32, so a sample never depends on call order, instance identity or worker. No unseeded entropy, no wall clock, no trigonometry in generation code. Note for future editors: world-a.terrain.test.ts scans source text, so the banned token strings must not appear under packages/world/src even inside comments; one red run was caused by a doc comment naming them.

The seed-sensitivity assertion in world-b.noise.test.ts is now exact: 200 of 200 samples must move when the seed changes. My first version relaxed it to more than 190 because samples on lattice lines collapse onto a single gradient component and tie across seeds. The stronger form keeps every sample strictly off-lattice (x on .25 or .75, z on .375 or .875) so all four cell gradients always contribute. That edit arrived from another process (see the next note), was reviewed, is in world-b's own file, and is adopted deliberately.

It was green when run (job fb72641699714420, 4 files / 61 tests) and contains no shell, network or filesystem-write code, only reads of src/noise. To adopt it deliberately: git checkout 5ab9f1d -- packages/world/src/__tests__/world-b.guards.test.ts (blob 4f75c8d0549152adfee4812908b9c7110013cd32). All four final gates were then re-run against 61d8159 and are the job ids listed above. Worth checking that no sibling task is writing or staging into another task's worktree.

Ownership respected: packages/core-types, docs/orchestration, root config, CI and all dependency declarations are untouched, no dependency was added or bumped, and the src/internal.ts constants were left to L1-A.
